column1: # 24장 말투 지시(11-10). 열: 조각 앞머리 → 지시(영어, 짧게). @scene 행은 장면 설명. 몬세의 편지(@letter)는 지시하지 않는다.

column2: Friday night at home. Montse, the landlady, tells Yuna they will go up to Montserrat tomorrow and asks her to bring the last of the old letters. Yuna has waited almost three months for this. Quiet, expectant.
calm and decided, an important invitation

Early Saturday. Montse and Yuna take the train to the mountain of Montserrat and the rack railway up to the monastery. Montse explains that her own name comes from the mountain: "Montserrat" means a mountain cut as if with a saw. They queue to see the small black Virgin, the Moreneta, and touch the ball in her hand. Calm, a little solemn; Yuna's hands are cold with nerves.
early morning, quietly expectant
awed, slowly
explaining the name, a little proud; stress "serrado" and "sierra"
quiet, nervous underneath
softly, near the statue; "Hoy, sí." almost to herself

A windy lookout high on Montserrat, a bench facing the void. Montse admits she wrote the last letter herself, signed only "M", in 2009, after her brother Martí died; Yuna reads it aloud in Spanish. Then Montse asks Yuna to forgive her for keeping it back, and tells her that Yuna's grandmother wrote back once, with a Korean word, "kwaenchanayo". Tender, grief and relief together.
quiet, wind and open space
a simple confession, quiet and steady
gentle, puzzled questions, not accusing

column1: M de Montse. Él me lo pidió.
column2: remembering her dying brother, tender; she quotes his words
warm, encouraging; "Ya puedes" proud of her

column1: 다 읽고 나서 나는 말을 할 수 없었다
column2: hushed, overwhelmed
an apology from the heart, voice unsteady; "Espero que me perdones, nena" softly
tender, a small smile through tears; she says the Korean word "Kwaenchanayo" carefully

Still on the mountain. Yuna asks Montse directly about Las Palmas and 1974, which worry her. Montse swears that Martí first met Yuna's grandmother in her own patio, not earlier, but says the papers, not her word, must prove it. Then a calm ride home, and a text message from Vale (the young Argentine lodger) saying an envelope from Korea has arrived.
firm but gentle, she needs the truth now
a solemn oath, steady, looking her in the eye
a small doubtful protest
understanding and calm; "Hay más cosas, nena" lower, keeping a secret kindly
calm, tired, at peace
reading Vale's text message, lightly amused, then expectant
